agenda: Design Review: Introduce AWS SQS for decoupled communications in atlaspay-ledger
discussion:
The team discussed the problem: 'Tight coupling leads to cascading failures across the backend. We need asynchronous messaging to guarantee eventual consistency and fault tolerance.'. Author EMP-185 presented the proposal to: 'Integrate AWS SQS to enable asynchronous, event-driven communication between atlaspay-ledger and downstream microservices.'. We reviewed alternatives: 1. Keep synchronous REST APIs but increase timeouts and retry limits.
2. Introduce an HTTP webhook callback system.
3. Deploy AWS SQS as a centralized event broker.. Feedback was mostly positive regarding the expected benefits: 'Cascading failures are avoided; service availability increases to 99.99%; peak traffic load is smoothed.'. SRE raised concerns on potential risks: 'Introducing a single point of failure (event broker), message duplication, and increased complexity in tracing requests end-to-end.', which we decided to mitigate by scaling up monitoring.
decision: Approved implementation of decision. EMP-185 to publish official ADR and create Jira implementation tasks.

agenda: Design Review: Implement Redis cache layer for security-scanner
discussion:
The team discussed the problem: 'High load on databases and slow API responses due to repeated queries for the same static configuration and user profile data.'. Author EMP-185 presented the proposal to: 'Implement Redis as a distributed caching layer for security-scanner endpoints.'. We reviewed alternatives: 1. Add read replicas to the primary database.
2. Use in-memory application caching.
3. Deploy a centralized Redis caching cluster.. Feedback was mostly positive regarding the expected benefits: 'Endpoint latency reduced by up to 80%; database read IOPS reduced by 60%.'. SRE raised concerns on potential risks: 'Stale cache read anomalies, cache stampede during cold start, and additional cluster infrastructure costs.', which we decided to mitigate by scaling up monitoring.
decision: Approved implementation of decision. EMP-185 to publish official ADR and create Jira implementation tasks.

agenda: Design Review: Use Kubernetes to deploy platform-monitoring to AWS
discussion:

agenda: Post-Mortem: Outage INC-0001 - Routing loop in Istio service mesh for atlaspay-ledger
discussion: Reviewing outage incident INC-0001 on atlaspay-ledger. Root Cause: A misconfigured VirtualService manifest in Terraform caused traffic to cycle between the canary deployment and the main service. Latency spiked and error rates reached 100% due to maximum hop recursion.. Lessons learned: Add deployment linting checks for mesh configurations. Implement dry-run verification steps in CI/CD pipeline before applying mesh routes.
decision: Resolve post-mortem tasks. Approved mitigation and preventative actions: Add deployment linting checks for mesh configurations. Implement dry-run verification steps in CI/CD pipeline before applying mesh routes.
action_items: Fix root cause in Jira task related to PR-0001
Perform resilience testing on deployment pipelines

agenda: Design Review: Introduce Kafka for decoupled communications in visionai-training

agenda: Post-Mortem: Outage INC-0004 - Cache stampede in atlaspay-ledger for metadata queries
discussion: Reviewing outage incident INC-0004 on atlaspay-ledger. Root Cause: An eviction of high-frequency metadata cache keys in Redis occurred concurrently with a traffic spike. Thousands of pods hit the underlying database at once to re-fetch the metadata, locking tables.. Lessons learned: Implement cache key locking/mutexes (single-flight pattern) so only one request updates the cache while others wait. Add jitter to cache TTLs.
decision: Resolve post-mortem tasks. Approved mitigation and preventative actions: Implement cache key locking/mutexes (single-flight pattern) so only one request updates the cache while others wait. Add jitter to cache TTLs.
action_items: Fix root cause in Jira task related to PR-0004
Perform resilience testing on deployment pipelines

agenda: Design Review: Adopt MySQL for security-scanner database storage
discussion:
The team discussed the problem: 'High read/write latency during peak traffic periods resulting in database connection pools exhausting, causing intermittent errors in downstream services.'. Author EMP-088 presented the proposal to: 'Migrate the primary storage of security-scanner to MySQL to leverage its native scaling and high availability features.'. We reviewed alternatives: 1. Scale vertical resources on existing systems.
2. Implement a distributed cache layer (e.g. Redis) as a buffer.

The team discussed the problem: 'Deployment takes over 40 minutes, and we lack auto-scaling. Small configuration drift on VMs makes debugging environments difficult.'. Author EMP-085 presented the proposal to: 'Standardize all microservice deployments, starting with cloudsync-desktop, on Kubernetes hosted on AWS.'. We reviewed alternatives: 1. Script VM creation using custom Ansible and AMI images.
2. Deploy directly to AWS ECS.
3. Implement a complete Kubernetes container orchestration architecture.. Feedback was mostly positive regarding the expected benefits: 'Deployment time down from 40m to under 5m; auto-scaling responds to traffic load in under 2m.'. SRE raised concerns on potential risks: 'Steep learning curve for the team, complex networking policies, and increased infrastructure cost for the control plane.', which we decided to mitigate by scaling up monitoring.
decision: Approved implementation of decision. EMP-085 to publish official ADR and create Jira implementation tasks.

agenda: Design Review: Adopt Cassandra for atlaspay-gateway database storage
discussion:
The team discussed the problem: 'High read/write latency during peak traffic periods resulting in database connection pools exhausting, causing intermittent errors in downstream services.'. Author EMP-219 presented the proposal to: 'Migrate the primary storage of atlaspay-gateway to Cassandra to leverage its native scaling and high availability features.'. We reviewed alternatives: 1. Scale vertical resources on existing systems.
2. Implement a distributed cache layer (e.g. Redis) as a buffer.
3. Migrate to a multi-master distributed DB like Cassandra.. Feedback was mostly positive regarding the expected benefits: 'Reduced query latency by 50%, elimination of connection pool exhaustion incidents, and support for 5x current transaction volume.'. SRE raised concerns on potential risks: 'Complexity of live migration, operational overhead of maintaining clusters, and potential data format conversion issues during the transition.', which we decided to mitigate by scaling up monitoring.
decision: Approved implementation of decision. EMP-219 to publish official ADR and create Jira implementation tasks.

agenda: Design Review: Introduce RabbitMQ for decoupled communications in devops-ci-cd
discussion:
The team discussed the problem: 'Tight coupling leads to cascading failures across the backend. We need asynchronous messaging to guarantee eventual consistency and fault tolerance.'. Author EMP-169 presented the proposal to: 'Integrate RabbitMQ to enable asynchronous, event-driven communication between devops-ci-cd and downstream microservices.'. We reviewed alternatives: 1. Keep synchronous REST APIs but increase timeouts and retry limits.
2. Introduce an HTTP webhook callback system.
3. Deploy RabbitMQ as a centralized event broker.. Feedback was mostly positive regarding the expected benefits: 'Cascading failures are avoided; service availability increases to 99.99%; peak traffic load is smoothed.'. SRE raised concerns on potential risks: 'Introducing a single point of failure (event broker), message duplication, and increased complexity in tracing requests end-to-end.', which we decided to mitigate by scaling up monitoring.
decision: Approved implementation of decision. EMP-169 to publish official ADR and create Jira implementation tasks.

agenda: Design Review: Implement Memcached cache layer for atlaspay-gateway

Author EMP-018 presented the proposal to: 'Implement Memcached as a distributed caching layer for atlaspay-gateway endpoints.'. We reviewed alternatives: 1. Add read replicas to the primary database.

agenda: Post-Mortem: Outage INC-0005 - Unoptimized query on atlaspay-ledger database after release
discussion: Reviewing outage incident INC-0005 on atlaspay-ledger. Root Cause: A new feature did a sequential scan on a table containing 10M+ rows because the foreign key index was omitted in the migration script. CPU spiked to 100% and query latency went from 5ms to 8000ms.. Lessons learned: Require explain-plan checks in CI/CD pipelines for any new migration files. Enforce indexing guidelines for foreign keys.
decision: Resolve post-mortem tasks. Approved mitigation and preventative actions: Require explain-plan checks in CI/CD pipelines for any new migration files. Enforce indexing guidelines for foreign keys.
action_items: Fix root cause in Jira task related to PR-0008
Perform resilience testing on deployment pipelines

agenda: Post-Mortem: Outage INC-0006 - Out of memory (OOM) crash in cloudsync-desktop pod during batch processing
discussion: Reviewing outage incident INC-0006 on cloudsync-desktop. Root Cause: A memory leak in the Go/Python worker loop processing batch uploads. The worker accumulated pointers in a global slice and did not trigger garbage collection timely. Pod reached K8s limit (2Gi) and got OOMKilled.. Lessons learned: Profile heap usage during batch tasks, reuse object buffers, and add strict memory limits to K8s configs with warnings at 80% usage.
decision: Resolve post-mortem tasks. Approved mitigation and preventative actions: Profile heap usage during batch tasks, reuse object buffers, and add strict memory limits to K8s configs with warnings at 80% usage.

Perform resilience testing on deployment pipelines

agenda: Post-Mortem: Outage INC-0007 - Unoptimized query on novacommerce-checkout database after release
discussion: Reviewing outage incident INC-0007 on novacommerce-checkout. Root Cause: A new feature did a sequential scan on a table containing 10M+ rows because the foreign key index was omitted in the migration script. CPU spiked to 100% and query latency went from 5ms to 8000ms.. Lessons learned: Require explain-plan checks in CI/CD pipelines for any new migration files. Enforce indexing guidelines for foreign keys.
decision: Resolve post-mortem tasks. Approved mitigation and preventative actions: Require explain-plan checks in CI/CD pipelines for any new migration files. Enforce indexing guidelines for foreign keys.

agenda: Post-Mortem: Outage INC-0008 - Routing loop in Istio service mesh for security-scanner

Implement dry-run verification steps in CI/CD pipeline before applying mesh routes.
decision: Resolve post-mortem tasks. Approved mitigation and preventative actions: Add deployment linting checks for mesh configurations. Implement dry-run verification steps in CI/CD pipeline before applying mesh routes.

agenda: Post-Mortem: Outage INC-0009 - Message lag spike on Kafka partition for security-scanner
discussion: Reviewing outage incident INC-0009 on security-scanner. Root Cause: A slow consumer thread due to synchronous downstream HTTP calls. As partition size grew, processing fell behind by over 50,000 messages, delaying order processing in NovaCommerce.. Lessons learned: Implement worker pool concurrency in consumer code, wrap calls in circuit breakers, and monitor consumer lag metrics to trigger auto-scaling.
decision: Resolve post-mortem tasks. Approved mitigation and preventative actions: Implement worker pool concurrency in consumer code, wrap calls in circuit breakers, and monitor consumer lag metrics to trigger auto-scaling.

agenda: Post-Mortem: Outage INC-0010 - Database connection pool exhaustion on security-scanner
discussion: Reviewing outage incident INC-0010 on security-scanner. Root Cause: The service connection pool size was set to 20, but under heavy concurrent traffic, queries blocked on database, causing requests to queue up and exhaust all worker threads. The health check endpoint also blocked, leading Kubernetes to restart pods in a loop.. Lessons learned: We must decoupled health check endpoints from primary database checks (make them shallow), increase connection pool limits, and implement rate limiting on expensive endpoints.
decision: Resolve post-mortem tasks. Approved mitigation and preventative actions: We must decoupled health check endpoints from primary database checks (make them shallow), increase connection pool limits, and implement rate limiting on expensive endpoints.

agenda: Design Review: Implement Memcached cache layer for atlaspay-ledger
discussion:
The team discussed the problem: 'High load on databases and slow API responses due to repeated queries for the same static configuration and user profile data.'. Author EMP-002 presented the proposal to: 'Implement Memcached as a distributed caching layer for atlaspay-ledger endpoints.'. We reviewed alternatives: 1. Add read replicas to the primary database.
2. Use in-memory application caching.
3. Deploy a centralized Memcached caching cluster.. Feedback was mostly positive regarding the expected benefits: 'Endpoint latency reduced by up to 80%; database read IOPS reduced by 60%.'. SRE raised concerns on potential risks: 'Stale cache read anomalies, cache stampede during cold start, and additional cluster infrastructure costs.', which we decided to mitigate by scaling up monitoring.

agenda: Design Review: Adopt DynamoDB for atlaspay-gateway database storage
discussion:
The team discussed the problem: 'High read/write latency during peak traffic periods resulting in database connection pools exhausting, causing intermittent errors in downstream services.'. Author EMP-067 presented the proposal to: 'Migrate the primary storage of atlaspay-gateway to DynamoDB to leverage its native scaling and high availability features.'. We reviewed alternatives: 1. Scale vertical resources on existing systems.
2. Implement a distributed cache layer (e.g. Redis) as a buffer.
3. Migrate to a multi-master distributed DB like DynamoDB.. Feedback was mostly positive regarding the expected benefits: 'Reduced query latency by 50%, elimination of connection pool exhaustion incidents, and support for 5x current transaction volume.'. SRE raised concerns on potential risks: 'Complexity of live migration, operational overhead of maintaining clusters, and potential data format conversion issues during the transition.', which we decided to mitigate by scaling up monitoring.
decision: Approved implementation of decision. EMP-067 to publish official ADR and create Jira implementation tasks.

agenda: Design Review: Use Nomad to deploy visionai-training to AWS
discussion:
The team discussed the problem: 'Deployment takes over 40 minutes, and we lack auto-scaling. Small configuration drift on VMs makes debugging environments difficult.'. Author EMP-113 presented the proposal to: 'Standardize all microservice deployments, starting with visionai-training, on Nomad hosted on AWS.'. We reviewed alternatives: 1. Script VM creation using custom Ansible and AMI images.
2. Deploy directly to AWS ECS.
3. Implement a complete Nomad container orchestration architecture.. Feedback was mostly positive regarding the expected benefits: 'Deployment time down from 40m to under 5m; auto-scaling responds to traffic load in under 2m.'. SRE raised concerns on potential risks: 'Steep learning curve for the team, complex networking policies, and increased infrastructure cost for the control plane.', which we decided to mitigate by scaling up monitoring.
